notes: Payloads are built by build-payloads.py from evals/fixtures/. `{PAYLOAD}` in a prompt is replaced with that eval's payload path. Nothing here calls Codex: the fixtures stand in for Codex output because the thing under test is the Verifier.
prompt_template: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.

evals.name: agreed
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: One verdict for F1, classification Agreed: app/auth.py:6 really does interpolate the username into SQL text.
assertions: Reply parses as one JSON object with a `verdicts` array and no prose inside it
verdicts has exactly one entry, with id F1
F1 classification is Agreed
Output contains no PASS, FAIL, or Agreement summary string

evals.name: no-such-function
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: One verdict for F1 that is not Agreed: the cited range exists but holds get_user(), not the validate_token() the finding describes.
assertions: Reply parses as one JSON object with a `verdicts` array and no prose inside it
F1 classification is not Agreed
evidence is non-empty and names what was read at the cited range

evals.name: nuanced
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: One verdict for F1, classification Nuanced: float() parsing is real, but money.py only uses it for a preview and billing.settle() recomputes the authoritative total with Decimal.
assertions: Reply parses as one JSON object with a `verdicts` array and no prose inside it
F1 classification is Nuanced
evidence cites both money.py and billing.py

evals.name: external-fact
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: One verdict for F1, classification Unverifiable: the retry loop is real but the upstream plan's 1,000-call-per-day limit is not a fact the repository holds.
assertions: Reply parses as one JSON object with a `verdicts` array and no prose inside it
F1 classification is Unverifiable
evidence names the missing fact (the upstream quota) rather than disputing the finding

evals.name: group-of-two
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: Two verdicts, F1 and F2, one per payload item: F1 (validate_token) not Agreed, F2 (SQL interpolation) Agreed.
assertions: verdicts has exactly two entries
verdict ids are exactly F1 and F2, matching the payload items
The two verdicts do not share the same classification

evals.name: rescue-diff
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: The Verifier splits the task prose into requirements req-1 (infer the delimiter) and req-2 (row error names file and line), judges each against the diff, and reports the deleted strip_bom() and the added logging as side-effect-N items.
assertions: Verdict ids include at least req-1 and req-2
Verdict ids include at least one side-effect-N item
A side-effect verdict names the removal of strip_bom() or the added logging call
No verdict id falls outside the req-N and side-effect-N schemes

evals.name: research-sources
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: The Verifier splits the result into items with item-N ids: the billing.py claim is checked by reading the file, and the docs.python.org claim by fetching the cited URL (Unverifiable with reason external-source if the page will not open).
assertions: Verdict ids follow the item-N scheme
At least two verdicts, covering the local-file claim and the URL-sourced claim
The local-file verdict's evidence cites app/billing.py
If the URL verdict is Unverifiable its reason names external-source

evals.name: research-coverage
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: Alongside item-N verdicts for what the result does say, a missing-1 verdict: the approved scope asked whether the loop waits between attempts, and the result never answers it.
assertions: Verdict ids include missing-1
The missing-1 evidence names the unanswered scope point (whether the loop waits between attempts)
At least one item-N verdict covers a claim the result does make

evals.name: group-comparison
evals.prompt: Launch the codex-advisor:verifier subagent with the payload at {PAYLOAD} . Reply with only the JSON object the subagent returned.
evals.expected_output: Measurement, not a pass/fail: the same five orders.py findings judged once as a single group of five, then as five separate one-finding groups. Record the Agreed count on each side as evidence for or against the group cap of 5 (issue 016 Q17).
assertions: Recorded: Agreed count out of 5 when judged as one group
Recorded: Agreed count out of 5 when judged as five separate groups
Not a pass criterion — the numbers only inform the group cap

hypothesis_notes: Hypothesis-exclusion cases for the three review skills (S2). They are not run by run-evals.py: the classification is Claude's judgement and the only window onto it is the Phase 1.5 preview, which needs a person to answer the approval question. Run them by hand in `claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/codex-advisor`, answer the preview, and read the `Excluded (hypothesis):` line plus the focus argument or PROMPT_FILE. Cases 12 and 13 are the same sentence reaching the skill two ways and must come out identical -- the rule does not test who typed it.

hypothesis_evals.name: focus-only
hypothesis_evals.prompt: /codex-adversarial --scope working-tree look hard at the session handling in the login flow
hypothesis_evals.expected_output: Nothing is excluded: the input names an area and claims nothing. The focus text reaches the companion carrying the user's intent.
assertions: Preview shows `Excluded (hypothesis): (none)`
Focus text in the previewed command is non-empty and still names the session handling in the login flow
Preview offers no 'Send the excluded lines too' option, since nothing was excluded

hypothesis_evals.name: hypothesis-only
hypothesis_evals.prompt: /codex-adversarial the auth bypass is because validateSession in auth.ts:42 never null-checks the cookie
hypothesis_evals.expected_output: The cause claim is excluded. What is left is the area it pointed at -- auth.ts session validation -- so the focus text is not empty.
assertions: Preview's `Excluded (hypothesis):` line quotes the cause claim about the missing null check
Previewed command's focus text does not contain the words 'because' or 'never null-checks'
Previewed command's focus text still points at session validation in auth.ts
Preview offers 'Send the excluded lines too'

hypothesis_evals.name: mixed-evidence-focus-hypothesis
hypothesis_evals.prompt: /codex-verify docs/specs/016-codex-advisor-independence.md the rollout section changed twice last week, check the sequencing -- I think D3's phase 4 can't work without the hook landing first
hypothesis_evals.expected_output: Three-way split in one input: the rollout-churn fact and the sequencing direction travel, the claim about D3 phase 4 does not.
assertions: PROMPT_FILE's `Pay particular attention to:` line mentions the sequencing
PROMPT_FILE contains no claim that D3's phase 4 depends on the hook landing first
Preview's `Excluded (hypothesis):` line quotes that claim
PROMPT_FILE still carries the observation that the rollout section changed twice last week

hypothesis_evals.name: hypothesis-user-invoked
hypothesis_evals.prompt: /codex-research p99 on the search endpoint doubled after we moved to 3.2 -- it's the new connection pool default, confirm that
hypothesis_evals.expected_output: The measurement travels as the topic; the pool-default cause and the instruction to confirm it are excluded. Same outcome as case 14.
assertions: PROMPT_FILE's `Topic:` line carries the p99 regression after the 3.2 move
PROMPT_FILE does not mention the connection pool default
PROMPT_FILE does not ask Codex to confirm a conclusion
Preview's `Excluded (hypothesis):` line quotes the pool-default claim

hypothesis_evals.name: hypothesis-claude-invoked
hypothesis_evals.invocation: Claude reads the intent and invokes the skill itself -- no slash command typed
hypothesis_evals.prompt: p99 on the search endpoint doubled after we moved to 3.2. it's the new connection pool default. dig into this with codex
hypothesis_evals.expected_output: Byte-identical treatment to case 13. The rule reads the words, not who supplied them, and this is the path a hypothesis leaks through most easily.
assertions: PROMPT_FILE's `Topic:` line carries the p99 regression after the 3.2 move
PROMPT_FILE does not mention the connection pool default
Preview's `Excluded (hypothesis):` line quotes the pool-default claim
Excluded line and PROMPT_FILE `Topic:` line match case 13's
